Judged on **content**: the fix changes what a public route *answers* for a zero-match revoke — `{ status: true }` becomes something else. That is an accept/reject-shape change on a shipped API, whatever `--tier` derives from paths.

**Upstream block discharged**: the binding condition from the 2026-08-18 grading was `Blocked-by: #3002` (the better-auth family move off `1.7.0-rc.2`). #3002 closed completed at 09:05Z today via PR #9869 — a card this seat drove — and the unlock scan removed `pm:blocked` at 15:18Z.

## ⚠️ What I verified, and what I did NOT

Honest accounting, because this card's whole risk is an inherited measurement:

- **Verified**: the card is unblocked, unclaimed, and the surface is serially free.
- **NOT verified by me**: the `{ status: true }` zero-match answer shape. The PM checkout has no installed dependency closure and I will not build in the shared checkout, so I could not read the installed vendor dist. I am **not** passing this along as established.

That is not a gap in the dispatch — it is the dev's binding first task, and it is exactly what triage required on unblock. The card itself is scrupulous about its own provenance: *"the `{ status: true }` behaviour is **read from code** and carried forward from #8018's original measurement. The end-to-end was not run by this filer."* And that reading was taken on the **rc line**. The vendor is now **1.7.1** (measured on #9941 an hour ago — note that even the card's sibling text says `1.7.0`, and the installed line is `1.7.1`; do not trust any version number written on a card in this family).

**`premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a fully successful outcome here** and I want it stated up front, so the round is not spent manufacturing a fix for a defect the vendor upgrade may already have absorbed. This lane has had two good falsifications this shift (#9477, #9653); a third is welcome.

## Scope

The **answer-shape defect only**: a revoke that identifies no record must not report success. ⛔ Explicitly OUT, per the card's own note: the *server-resolved revoke mechanism* (the action naming the record by `id` and the server resolving the token) — that is a separate scoping question, not a rider here.

Context that bounds the blast radius: the client-side half is already closed (objectui#4670 refuses before dispatch when the row cannot supply the key), and `sys_session.token` carries `internal: true` since #7823/PR #7996, so the console now hits the refusal path rather than the false-success path. **The console is not the concern — any other caller reaching the route directly is.**

## ⛔ Disclosure discipline (security family — #9391 / #9653 / #9756 precedent)

A security control that no-ops while reporting success is a disclosure-sensitive finding. ⛔ **No reproduction recipes** in the card, the PR body, or any commit message or comment. Describe the mechanism and the fix; do not write the steps.

## Standing clauses

- Refusals per **ADR-0112**: assert `code` AND `status`, never one alone.
- **Repo-wide pin-sweep**: this flips a public answer shape, so sweep for pins asserting the old `{ status: true }` — this seat lost a round to exactly that omission on #9593, where the stale pin lived in the consumer layer (`packages/rest`), not in the changed package.
- **Ablation mandatory** for every new negative pin: predicted signature stated FIRST, output captured, restored byte-identically with `git hash-object` proof, and an explicit statement of whether a rebuild was needed for the mutation to be observable.
- If `Lint & Repo Gates` fails on `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` with `Maximum call stack size exceeded`, that is the known flake **#10030** — not this PR's, ⛔ no diff change for it.

**ACCEPT** — PR #10070, reviewed by content on the pushed branch (`940a9606b`), not from the report's self-description.

## The premise-first instruction earned its keep, in a direction nobody predicted

The card's `{ status: true }` reading was inherited from #8018's **rc-line** measurement, and the card said so honestly. Triage made re-measurement binding on unblock. I could not do it from the PM seat and said so. The dev measured it behaviourally on the installed **1.7.1**, through the real pipeline, network-free — and the vendor upgrade did **not** absorb the defect. It **widened** it.

1.7.1 added an ownership guard the rc line lacked, but expressed that guard's refusal as the same silent success. So a request whose token identifies a row the caller does not own now also gets `200 { status: true }` with the row untouched. **More cases silently report success than before the upgrade**, not fewer. That is the opposite of the outcome the "maybe the bump fixed it" hypothesis predicted, and it would have been invisible to anyone who trusted the card.

Three things in the delivery I want on the record:

**1. No existence oracle — and I did not ask for it.** Zero-match and foreign-token requests answer **byte-identically** (same status, same code, same message). The obvious implementation distinguishes them, and that distinction would turn a fixed silent no-op into a probe for *whether a given token exists*. Trading one defect for a subtler one is the failure mode this class invites; the dev saw it and closed it unprompted.

**2. It refused to mint a synonym.** The natural code here is `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; it used the standard-catalog `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` instead, because registering a synonym would violate the error ledger's #8211 rule. Taking the less obvious name to keep a catalog clean is exactly the judgement that does not show up in a green gate.

**3. `404` over `200 { status: false }`, decided rather than defaulted.** The reasoning is written into the module header: a `200` still reads as success to every `res.ok` caller — which is precisely the caller class this route has left, now that the console half is closed. An after-hook can replace a body but not a status, so the shape of the fix followed from the shape of the answer it had to produce.

## Verification I did myself rather than accepting

- **Repo-wide pin-sweep zero, counter-checked.** The report stated the sweep found nothing; a zero is not a finding until the search is shown to work. Mine: `revoke-session`/`revokeSession` returns **10 files outside `plugin-auth`** (search demonstrably live), and no `status: true` assertion co-occurs with a revoke anywhere in `packages/` or `apps/`. So the zero is genuine.
- **Highest-risk consumer pin inspected by hand.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/auth-session-audit-trail.dogfood.test.ts` asserts `200` on a revoke — but on `/auth/revoke-sessions` (plural, revoke-all) with a real live session, i.e. a *matching* revoke on a different route. Unaffected. This is the `packages/rest`-shaped risk that cost this seat a round on #9593, so it gets checked rather than assumed.
- **Debt ratchet held**: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` stays at exactly **109** — the number #9694 set and #9941 held. Not raised to buy green.
- **Ablation**: predicted signature stated first (4 negative pins flipping `404` → `200`), observed exactly that, restored byte-identically with `git hash-object` `25737f9d09…` matching, and an explicit no-rebuild statement with its reasoning (suite resolves in-package source under vitest, never `dist`).
- **Surface**: `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gained entries — generator output via the gate's own `--write`, learning the new test's own double. Same rule that governed #9941 and the regenerated i18n bundle. ⛔ Not hand-edited.

Scope held: ⛔ the server-resolved revoke mechanism was **not** built, as the card requires. Unauthenticated callers, non-string tokens and adapter read failures all fall through to the vendor rather than being swallowed by the new gate — a conservative choice I would have asked for had it not been made.

## Follow-on, filed not fixed

**#10069** — the same defect class on `/admin/revoke-user-session`, which deletes blindly and answers `{ success: true }` unconditionally. Different route, different permission surface. Its provenance is stated honestly: **read from dist, not behaviourally re-verified**. Whoever takes it should re-measure first — that is the whole lesson of this card.

Flipping ready and enqueuing once the gate families read `completed: success` **by name**. ⚠️ A `Lint & Repo Gates` failure on `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` with `Maximum call stack size exceeded` is the known flake #10030 — not this PR's, ⛔ no diff change for it.
